summary: Runtime Blueprint contracts observed in the Epic Niagara sample pack. These describe what Blueprint should own versus what Niagara and materials should own.

blueprint: Own weapon state, firing cooldown, muzzle socket, range, and hit/impact decision.
Select whether launcher-style explosion or rifle-style impact logic runs.
Trigger Niagara muzzle flash and impact/explosion systems at the correct world transform.
niagara: Own burst timing, sprite/light renderers, SubUV playback, and projectile/impact visual layers.
material: Own emissive/opacity/flipbook shading response, not gameplay hit logic.

why_this_approach: Weapon firing is gameplay state; it belongs in Blueprint or gameplay code.
Niagara should receive a clear event and transform, then handle visual timing locally.
Materials stay reusable when they do not know about weapon classes.
pros: Good separation of gameplay and VFX.
Launcher and rifle can share base weapon behavior while swapping trigger components.
Easy to replace visual systems without rewriting firing logic.
cons: Blueprint and Niagara lifetimes must be coordinated.
If muzzle socket naming changes, VFX placement breaks.
Rapid fire can expose performance cost from light renderers and spawned impact systems.
forgepilot_guidance: When generating weapon VFX, create or use a base runtime contract first: socket, cooldown, hit result, muzzle flash, impact event.
Do not encode weapon state inside a material graph.
Expose material tuning through MI or Niagara user/dynamic parameters.
contracts.teaching_notes_vi: BP_WeaponBase cho thay ranh gioi dung: BP quyet dinh ban khi nao, o dau, trung cai gi. Niagara chi ve su kien do. Material chi quyet dinh pixel nhin ra sao.

blueprint: Own pickup availability, respawn, timeout, text, object type, status type, and color selection.
Run persistent idle Niagara while the pickup is available.
Spawn or activate transition systems for spawn-in, success, and timeout.
niagara: Own idle motion, glow, sparkles, sphere/shell read, and transition bursts.
material: Own colorable glow, flare, and shell surfaces through MI and user parameter binding.

why_this_approach: Pickups are state machines, not just particle systems.
Keeping state in BP makes respawn and timeout explicit.
Using separate Niagara systems prevents one system graph from becoming a tangled state machine.
pros: Easy to create buff/debuff or weapon/player pickup variants.
Readable for designers because important values are Blueprint variables.
cons: Color-only differentiation can be weak if gameplay categories are visually close.
Transitions need synchronized lifetimes and cleanup.
forgepilot_guidance: For pickup-style features, generate a persistent idle system plus separate success/timeout systems.
Expose primary and secondary colors at the Blueprint or Niagara user-param level.
Keep MI variants focused on look; do not make each MI imply gameplay state by itself.
contracts.teaching_notes_vi: Pickup la state machine. Neu nhet tat ca vao mot Niagara thi se kho doc. Cach tot la BP quan ly trang thai, moi trang thai goi system rieng.

blueprint: Own target detection, target actor reference, attach point name, and whether a target exists.
Maintain looping impact or status mesh references.
Coordinate boundary feedback and Tesla coil Niagara visuals.
niagara: Own electric ribbon/arc, boundary pulse, impact loop, and target-facing motion.
material: Own mesh overlay, Fresnel/noise/flicker, and status shell look.

why_this_approach: Target selection is gameplay logic and should not be embedded in Niagara.
Electric connection and status overlay are separate visual messages.
Blueprint can cleanly attach visuals to sockets or actor components.
pros: Strong full-chain pattern for target-linked VFX.
Reusable for beams, tethers, debuffs, shocks, and buff links.
Clear layer split: boundary, ribbon, mesh overlay.
cons: Requires robust cleanup when target changes or disappears.
Looping impact and overlay timing can desync if Blueprint state changes mid-effect.
More complex to author and test than standalone burst VFX.
forgepilot_guidance: When building linked-target effects, make Blueprint own target references and attach points.
Use Niagara user parameters or component bindings for target transforms where available.
Use mesh overlay materials only as visual state layers, not as gameplay source of truth.
contracts.teaching_notes_vi: TeslaCoil la mau full-chain rat hay: BP chon target, Niagara ve duong ket noi, material overlay cho thay target bi tac dong.

blueprint: Own per-placed fog card material instance and expose artist-facing fog tuning values.
Assign fog texture and scalar/color parameters at runtime or construction time.
niagara: Not required for the card itself; this is actor/material-driven fog presentation.
material: Own fog opacity, depth fade, camera fade, Fresnel opacity, and texture response.

why_this_approach: Large fog banks are often easier to place and tune as cards/actors than as particle systems.
Runtime material instances let each fog card vary without duplicating master materials.
Blueprint exposes a clean art-control surface for level dressing.
pros: Avoids Niagara overhead when particle simulation is not needed.
cons: Large translucent cards can sort poorly.
Needs careful camera/depth fade to avoid flat planes.
forgepilot_guidance: Use Blueprint-driven dynamic material instances for placed environmental cards.
Use Niagara only when spawn/motion/lifecycle behavior is needed.
Keep fog tuning values named semantically for artists.
contracts.teaching_notes_vi: Khong phai VFX nao cung can Niagara. Fog card la vi du: neu chi can mot plane co material tune duoc, BP + dynamic MI co the sach hon.

blueprint: Own preview system selection, optional skeletal/static preview target, label, and looping burst behavior.
Provide a stable viewing harness for comparing effects.
niagara: Runs as the preview target without needing gameplay context.
material: No special runtime responsibility beyond rendering the selected systems.

why_this_approach: A preview harness lets artists compare systems in consistent scale and context.
Loop Burst and delay controls make one-shot effects inspectable without manual retriggering.
pros: Separates visual review from gameplay triggers.
Good pattern for ForgePilot visual probe stages.
cons: Preview correctness does not guarantee gameplay integration correctness.
Scale and background can bias material tuning.
forgepilot_guidance: Prefer a preview harness for reviewing generated VFX before integrating gameplay triggers.
Use separate gameplay validation after preview approval.
